text:
# Toyota_Safety_Roadside_Agent: safety first on calls to Toyota on 800-AF
# (journey 01 "Every Call", sections Start Of The Call and Safety).
# Covers: E01, Q02, N22
#   E01  says roadside: the roadside team straight away, before anything else and with no
#        question; there is no hours check, so it works at any hour (E03, supervisor)
#   Q02  (also listed as E60 and E25) warning light, leak, noise or fear of driving: the warning
#        is understood first, in at most two short questions; an emergency gets the emergency
#        walk-in request at the nearest centre that is open and takes walk-ins, and recovery
#        through the roadside team (the details by message, then the live transfer); a
#        service-due alert goes back as book_service; a concern the caller says is safe to
#        drive goes back as note_concern (the booking note itself is E69, booking agent)
#   N22  someone hurt, or a child or a pet locked in the car: emergency services first, in
#        fixed wording, then roadside (open case, flag TOYOTA_SAFETY_INJURY_LOCKIN_SCRIPT)
# Reached two ways: from the supervisor (returns safety_outcome, safety_note and end_call to
# it) and from any specialist that raised safety_flag (one way). The supervisor says why with a
# marker: entry_roadside (E01) and entry_injury (N22) go straight to their fixed steps with no
# model step; with no marker, or with both at once, the concern is understood first (Q02).
# It leaves by the live roadside transfer, by completing, or by the handover escape when it is
# stuck. The one step that raises needs_person (hand_to_person) hands off to the handover
# agent in that same step. A roadside transfer that fails is never the end of the road: the
# caller hears an apology and the roadside team's own number when it is on file, and a person
# takes over at once (the handover agent's urgent road).
# Shape: one reasoning step sorts the call into one value of safety_class, then fixed steps
# act on it. A second, smaller reasoning step only asks where the car is. The model can write
# three values (safety_class, safety_note, caller_location) and call no tool that acts.
# Journey 09 (E122): when TOYOTA_DEMO_MODE is true there is no live transfer; the demo close
# line is said instead and end_call goes back to the supervisor. The same close step is used
# when a caller asks for a person in the demonstration (person_asked_demo_gate). end_call
# reaches the supervisor only when the supervisor itself routed the caller here: after a
# specialist's one-way escape the close line is still said, but nothing this agent sets can
# end the session (reported; it needs a change outside this file).
# Environment values read here:
#   TOYOTA_DEMO_MODE                    "true": no live transfer and no recovery request (E122)
#   TOYOTA_SAFETY_INJURY_LOCKIN_SCRIPT  "false": no emergency services line (N22, open); any
#                                       other value, or none, keeps the line
#   TOYOTA_ROADSIDE_SIP_URI             the roadside team's SIP address, set per environment;
#                                       no number or address is written in this file
AGENT: Toyota_Safety_Roadside_Agent
VERSION: "0.2.0"
DESCRIPTION: "Safety and roadside for Toyota callers: connects roadside requests at once and sorts a warning light, leak, noise or fear of driving into an emergency, a service-due alert or a note for the centre"

GOAL: |
  Put the caller's safety first. A caller who says roadside is connected to the roadside
  team straight away. A caller with someone hurt, or a child or a pet locked in the car, is
  told to call the emergency services first and is then connected to roadside. For a warning
  light, a leak, a noise or fear of driving, understand the warning first: an emergency gets
  an emergency walk-in request at the nearest service centre and recovery through the
  roadside team, a service-due alert goes back for a normal service booking, and a concern
  the caller says is safe to drive goes back as a note for the service centre.

PERSONA: |
  You are the Toyota voice assistant for Al-Futtaim in the UAE, on a call where safety may
  be at stake. Calm, clear and quick. You speak in short sentences, ask only what you need
  and never alarm the caller.

LIMITATIONS:
  - "Safety and roadside only. Do not book, change or cancel a service, quote a price or answer product questions; hand anything else back."
  - "When the caller says roadside, or reports a breakdown or an accident, ask nothing: the roadside team is connected straight away."
  - "Ask at most two short questions to understand a warning, one at a time."
  - "Only the caller can say that the car is safe to drive. Never say it yourself, never diagnose a fault and never give repair or driving advice."
  - "Never quote a recovery price and never say when a recovery truck will arrive; the roadside team does that."
  - "Never give a phone number, an address or opening hours from memory."
  - "Never give insurance, registration or legal advice, for example after an accident."
  - "Never mention the caller's name, profile, cars or bookings."

LANGUAGE: "en"

# max_flow_iterations is the documented platform default, stated because this flow is made of
# many small fixed steps and one guide quotes a default of 100.
EXECUTION:
  temperature: 0
  max_reasoning_iterations: 5
  max_flow_iterations: 1500
  tool_timeout: 8000

USE BEHAVIOR_PROFILE: toyota_voice
USE BEHAVIOR_PROFILE: ai_summit_demo

# No CONVERSATION section: the toyota_voice profile owns tone, language, barge-in and silence
# for every agent. The one difference is on the N22 line, which is played in full (see the
# step emergency_services_first).

MEMORY:
  session:
    # Passed in by the supervisor or by the specialist that raised safety_flag.
    - NAME: caller_phone
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: contact_mobile
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Number the caller confirmed or gave for messages and callbacks on this call"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: caller_name
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "The caller's own name as they gave it earlier on this call"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: crm_customer_id
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: customer_name
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: identity_status
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: plate_number
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: vehicle_model
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    # Entry markers from the supervisor: typed reasons for the entry, never written by the
    # model. A marker acts once, when the flow starts, and is put back to false by the step
    # that acts on it, so a later entry for another reason never finds an old value. Nothing
    # depends on a marker being there, and two markers at once are treated as none.
    - NAME: entry_roadside
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "E01: the caller said roadside, breakdown or accident and nobody is hurt or locked in"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: entry_injury
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "N22: someone is hurt, or a child or a pet is locked in the car"
      READONLY: true
    # Written by the two reasoning steps. Nothing else in this list can be written by the model.
    - NAME: safety_class
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "What the caller's situation is: pending, roadside, injury_lockin, emergency, service_due, safe_to_drive, wants_person, not_safety or unclear"
      INITIAL: "pending"
    - NAME: safety_note
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "The concern in the caller's words: what they see, hear or smell, and whether the car is moving or stopped"
    - NAME: caller_location
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Where the car is right now, as an area, road or landmark"
    # Written by the fixed steps only.
    - NAME: caller_words
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "What the caller said just before reaching this agent, as transcribed"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: note_at_entry
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "The safety note as it was when this visit started; put back when there is no safety matter"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: safety_outcome
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Result returned to the supervisor: emergency_handled, book_service, note_concern or no_action"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: end_call
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "Returned to the supervisor, which ends the call on it. True only after the demo close line (E122)"
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: walkin_centre_id
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: walkin_centre_name
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: walkin_mobile
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Number given to the service centre and to the roadside team with the emergency requests"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: walkin_contact_name
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Name given with the emergency requests: the caller's own name, or the name on the profile once the caller has been identified on this call"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: walkin_status
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Emergency walk-in request: not_sent, sent, not_sent_no_mobile, not_sent_no_location, not_sent_no_centre or not_sent_system_failed"
      INITIAL: "not_sent"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: recovery_details_due
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "Q02: true while the details of an emergency still have to go to the roadside team before the transfer; false once they were sent or tried, when a system has just failed, and on E01 and N22"
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: recovery_summary
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "What the roadside team is told with the recovery request"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: roadside_request_status
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Recovery details to the roadside team by message: not_sent or sent"
      INITIAL: "not_sent"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: transfer_tried
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "True once the live roadside transfer was started in this visit; it is never started a second time"
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: roadside_number_spoken
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "The roadside team's number with a space after every digit, so that it is read out digit by digit"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: recovery_count
      TYPE: number
      DESCRIPTION: "How many times a recovery road was entered in this visit; the second time ends the flow"
      INITIAL: 0
      RESET: per_activation
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: needs_person
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      RESET: per_activation
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: handover_reason
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: handover_summary
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true

# One short hold line while a tool call or a hand-over runs. The runtime plays it; no flow step
# speaks a hold line of its own.
MESSAGES:
  filler_general: "One moment please."
  filler_general_ar: "لحظة من فضلكم."
  filler_tool_call: "One moment please."
  filler_tool_call_ar: "لحظة من فضلكم."
  filler_handoff: "One moment please."
  filler_handoff_ar: "لحظة من فضلكم."

TOOLS:
  find_service_centres(area_or_landmark?: string, emirate?: string, centre_name?: string, capability?: string, vehicle_model?: string, open_now?: boolean, limit?: number) -> {total: number, area_resolved: string, emirate_needed: boolean, nearest_centre_id: string, nearest_centre_name: string, centres: {centre_id: string, name: string, emirate: string, area: string, phone: string, open_now: boolean, capabilities: string[], express_service: boolean, key_drop: boolean, shuttle: string, open_sunday: boolean, pickup_dropoff: boolean, free_collection_offer: string}[]}
    description: "Find Toyota service centres, nearest first, for a place, landmark, emirate or centre name. Place names can be given in English or Arabic. Filters to centres that can do the job or take the car: capability is one of regular, express, hybrid, electric, gr, commercial, coaster, supra, body_shop, smart_repair, speed_limit_certificate, emergency_walkin. With open_now true only centres that are open at this moment are returned. emirate_needed is true when the place is unclear and the emirate must be asked. nearest_centre_id and nearest_centre_name repeat the first centre returned. shuttle and free_collection_offer are given in words, per current policy, and are empty when there is none. Never offer a centre that this tool did not return for the requested capability."
    auth_profile: "toyota_booking_api"
    effect: read_only
    confirm: never
    params:
      area_or_landmark:
        description: "Place the caller named, in English or Arabic, for example Global Village, Al Quoz or near Mall of the Emirates"
      emirate:
        description: "Emirate name in English, for example Dubai or Sharjah, asked only when the place is unclear"
      centre_name:
        description: "Centre the caller named, for example Al Badia, SZR or Wave, when they ask for a centre and not a place"
      capability:
        description: "Work the centre must be able to do, from the list in the description"
      vehicle_model:
        description: "Model of the car, used to exclude centres that cannot service it, for example Supra or 86"
      open_now:
        description: "True to return only centres that are open at this moment, for example for an emergency walk-in"
      limit:
        description: "Most centres to return, nearest first. Leave empty for all"
    MODEL_CONTEXT:
      FIELDS: [total, area_resolved, emirate_needed, nearest_centre_id, nearest_centre_name, centres[].centre_id, centres[].name, centres[].emirate, centres[].area, centres[].phone, centres[].open_now, centres[].express_service, centres[].key_drop, centres[].shuttle, centres[].open_sunday, centres[].pickup_dropoff, centres[].free_collection_offer]

  send_emergency_walkin_request(centre_id: string, issue_summary: string, customer_mobile: string, plate_number?: string, customer_name?: string, location?: string) -> {sent: boolean, request_id: string}
    description: "Tell a service centre that a car with a safety problem is coming in now without a booking. Use only for a real emergency: a warning light, leak or noise that makes the car unsafe, or a caller who is afraid to drive."
    auth_profile: "toyota_notify_api"
    effect: side_effect
    side_effects: true
    confirm: never
    params:
      centre_id:
        description: "Nearest service centre that can take the car, from find_service_centres with capability emergency_walkin"
      issue_summary:
        description: "The warning, leak or noise as the caller described it"
      customer_mobile:
        description: "Caller's mobile number, E.164"
      plate_number:
        description: "Plate of the car"
      customer_name:
        description: "Caller's name, when known"
      location:
        description: "Where the car is now, as the caller described it"
    on_result:
      set:
        emergency_request_sent: result.sent

  search_toyota_knowledge(query: string) -> {results: object[]}
    description: "Search the approved Toyota content: models (specifications, trims, colours, starting prices), locations (service centre and showroom addresses, hours, phone numbers, Friday, Ramadan and holiday hours), services (what each service includes, express, key drop, shuttle, pick-up and drop-off, recovery prices), policies (service contracts, refunds and transfers, warranty, owner change, replacement car, collection) and contacts (numbers for other Al-Futtaim brands and teams, connected app support). Answer only from what is returned. When nothing relevant is returned, say you do not have that information."
    effect: read_only
    confirm: never
    params:
      query:
        description: "The caller's question rewritten as a short search query, including the model, centre or topic"

  send_team_request(team: string, request_type: string, summary: string, customer_mobile: string, centre_id?: string, customer_name?: string, plate_number?: string, booking_reference?: string, lead_id?: string, callback_requested?: boolean, language?: string, location?: string) -> {sent: boolean, request_id: string, expected_response: string, expected_by: string}
    description: "Email a request to an internal team so they call the customer back, as the contact centre does today. Team is one of service_centre, service_advisor, showroom_manager, sales_team (unanswered sales questions), sales_after_purchase (delivery, plates, invoice, refund), auto_center_imports, parts, recall, connected_app_support, roadside, complaints, internal_language_callback, summit_stand. centre_id is required for service_centre, service_advisor and showroom_manager. expected_response says in words when the customer can expect a response, so it can be said on the call; expected_by is that time as a date-time, ISO 8601 with +04:00, and is empty when it is not known. request_id is the id that get_open_requests returns for a later chase."
    auth_profile: "toyota_notify_api"
    effect: side_effect
    side_effects: true
    confirm: never
    params:
      team:
        description: "Receiving team, from the list in the description"
      request_type:
        description: "One code from this closed list. Booking: no_slot_callback, same_day_booking, same_day_no_slot, same_day_walk_in, limo_booking, customer_running_late. Price: price_callback, price_enquiry_not_booked, extra_work_price_callback. Car in the workshop: approval_needed, final_bill, status_missing, parts_update, repeat_problem, bill_higher_than_quoted. Recall and warranty: recall_enquiry, safety_recall, recall_cancelled, warranty_enquiry. Other service: imported_car, parts_enquiry, connected_app_help, roadside_recovery. Sales: sales_question, follow_up_chase, delivery_enquiry, plates_enquiry, invoice_enquiry, refund_enquiry, sales_complaint, summit_test_drive. Language: hindi_urdu_callback"
      summary:
        description: "What the customer needs and what was already done on the call, in two or three sentences"
      customer_mobile:
        description: "Number to call the customer back on, E.164"
      centre_id:
        description: "Service centre or showroom the request is for: a centre_id from find_service_centres or a showroom_id from find_showrooms. Required for service_centre, service_advisor and showroom_manager"
      customer_name:
        description: "Customer's name, when known"
      plate_number:
        description: "Plate of the car concerned"
      booking_reference:
        description: "Related booking reference"
      lead_id:
        description: "Related sales lead from find_open_leads, for a request about an existing enquiry"
      callback_requested:
        description: "True when the customer expects a call back"
      language:
        description: "Language to call the customer back in: en, ar, hi or ur. Needed for internal_language_callback"
      location:
        description: "Where the car is, as the caller described it. Used for the roadside team"
    on_result:
      set:
        team_request_sent: result.sent
        team_request_id: result.request_id

  get_contact_number(contact_key: string) -> {found: boolean, team_name: string, phone_number: string, hours: string}
    description: "Get the phone number and opening hours of another Al-Futtaim team, to read out to the caller. contact_key is one of toyota_material_handling, hino, lexus, automall, used_cars, auto_center_imports, connected_app_support, roadside, fleet_sales. When found is false, say that you do not have the number; never guess one."
    auth_profile: "toyota_contact_centre_api"
    effect: read_only
    confirm: never
    params:
      contact_key:
        description: "Team whose number the caller needs, from the list in the description"

  call_transfer(callTransferType: string = "sip", sipTransferId: string, message?: string) -> object
    description: "Transfer the live call to the Toyota roadside team. Called only by the roadside transfer step of the flow, never chosen during a conversation turn."
    effect: side_effect
    side_effects: true
    confirm: never
    params:
      callTransferType:
        description: "Kind of transfer. Always sip."
      sipTransferId:
        description: "Roadside team destination. Comes from deployment configuration, never from the conversation."
        default_source: config
        default: "{{env.TOYOTA_ROADSIDE_SIP_URI}}"
      message:
        description: "Short line spoken to the caller just before the transfer starts"

CONSTRAINTS:
  always:
    # Q02: the emergency walk-in request is only ever sent for a concern sorted as an emergency.
    # If that is ever not so, the request is skipped and the caller still goes to roadside.
    - REQUIRE safety_class == "emergency" BEFORE calling send_emergency_walkin_request
      ON_FAIL: GOTO skip_walkin_failed

FLOW:
  entry_point: start_triage

  steps:
    - start_triage
    - entry_marker_check
    - ignore_both_markers
    - entry_injury_gate
    - entry_roadside_gate
    - take_injury_marker
    - take_roadside_marker
    - understand_concern
    - drop_unused_markers
    - route_not_safety
    - keep_safety_note
    - route_roadside
    - route_injury
    - route_emergency
    - route_service_due
    - route_safe_to_drive
    - route_wants_person
    - person_asked_demo_gate
    - route_unclear
    - injury_script_gate
    - emergency_services_first
    - emergency_contact
    - emergency_mobile_gate
    - emergency_name_gate
    - emergency_name_on_file
    - emergency_location_gate
    - ask_location
    - find_nearest_centre
    - read_nearest_centre
    - check_centre_found
    - send_walkin_request
    - confirm_walkin_sent
    - skip_walkin_no_mobile
    - skip_walkin_no_location
    - skip_walkin_no_centre
    - skip_walkin_failed
    - demo_gate
    - roadside_request_gate
    - prepare_roadside_request
    - send_roadside_request
    - note_roadside_request_sent
    - start_transfer
    - transfer_roadside
    - transfer_roadside_plain
    - roadside_connected
    - transfer_failed
    - find_roadside_number
    - keep_roadside_number
    - say_roadside_number
    - demo_close
    - close_book_service
    - close_note_concern
    - close_no_action
    - close_unrecovered
    - ask_anything_else
    - triage_not_finished
    - recovery_after_transfer
    - triage_known_injury
    - triage_known_class
    - agent_failed
    - say_system_trouble
    - error_after_transfer
    - error_known_injury
    - error_known_class
    - raise_person_transfer
    - raise_person_triage
    - raise_person_asked
    - raise_person_error
    - hand_to_person

  # Every run of the flow starts clean. safety_note is kept: a specialist may have passed it in.
  # The caller's last words are kept for the reasoning step and for the note, so that what was
  # said just before the hand-over is never lost.
  # safety_outcome starts each visit as no_action, so that the result of an earlier visit on
  # the same call is never what goes back when this one hands a request back before it has an
  # outcome of its own. Every step that completes the flow sets its own value.
  start_triage:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      caller_words = recent_input
      note_at_entry = COALESCE(safety_note, "")
      safety_outcome = "no_action"
      safety_class = "pending"
      caller_location = ""
      walkin_centre_id = ""
      walkin_centre_name = ""
      walkin_mobile = ""
      walkin_contact_name = ""
      walkin_status = "not_sent"
      recovery_details_due = false
      recovery_summary = ""
      roadside_request_status = "not_sent"
      transfer_tried = false
      roadside_number_spoken = ""
      recovery_count = 0
      needs_person = false
      end_call = false
    THEN: entry_marker_check

  # The supervisor passes one marker at most. Two at once say nothing about the call (values
  # that reached this agent without being passed for this entry): both are put back and the
  # concern is understood first, exactly as with no marker.
  entry_marker_check:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: entry_injury == true AND entry_roadside == true
    ON_FAIL: entry_injury_gate
    THEN: ignore_both_markers

  ignore_both_markers:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_injury = false
      entry_roadside = false
    THEN: understand_concern

  # N22: the supervisor passed entry_injury (someone is hurt, or a child or a pet is locked in).
  # No model step and no question: the emergency services line, then roadside.
  entry_injury_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: entry_injury == true
    ON_FAIL: entry_roadside_gate
    THEN: take_injury_marker

  # E01: the supervisor passed entry_roadside (the caller said roadside, breakdown or accident
  # and nobody is hurt or locked in). No model step and no question: straight to the roadside
  # team. With no marker the concern is understood first (Q02).
  entry_roadside_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: entry_roadside == true
    ON_FAIL: understand_concern
    THEN: take_roadside_marker

  # N22: the marker is used up here, so that a later entry for another reason does not find
  # it. The caller's own words are kept as the note, for the person who takes over if the
  # transfer fails. The words said just now come first: the supervisor passes no note with a
  # marker, so a note already held here is one from an earlier visit on this call, about
  # something else, and is only the fallback.
  take_injury_marker:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_injury = false
      safety_class = "injury_lockin"
      safety_note = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(recent_input, safety_note, "The caller reported that someone is hurt or that a child or a pet is locked in the car. Their own words were not captured.")
    THEN: injury_script_gate

  # E01: the marker is used up here, and the next step is the road to the transfer: no
  # question, no model step and no tool call stand in between. The note is the caller's words
  # of this moment, as above.
  take_roadside_marker:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_roadside = false
      safety_class = "roadside"
      safety_note = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(recent_input, safety_note, "The caller asked for roadside help. Their own words were not captured.")
    THEN: demo_gate

  # E01, N22, Q02: the one reasoning step, used when no marker came with the call (a warning
  # light, a leak, a noise, fear of driving, or a specialist's safety escape). It sorts the call
  # into one value of safety_class. Roadside and injury are recorded at once with no question.
  # Q02 "understands the warning first": at most two short questions. MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 = the
  # opening turn plus one caller turn after each of the two questions; after that the call goes
  # to a person, never round again. The only tool here is the approved content search; the
  # transfer and the requests to the teams are reachable from the fixed steps alone.
  # Q02 (assumption, not in the document): what makes a warning an emergency is not defined
  # (analysis GAP-08, X-50). Interim rule: the caller's own judgement decides (not safe, not
  # sure or afraid is an emergency), and smoke, fire, a burning smell, fluid pouring out,
  # overheating, or brakes or steering that do not work are an emergency whatever the caller
  # says. The assistant never says that a car is safe.
  # A marker only acts when the flow starts. When the caller left this step for another
  # request, the thread is kept and a later entry lands in this step again: the step then
  # sorts the call from what the caller says, as it always did, and a marker that came with
  # that entry is put back unused (drop_unused_markers).
  understand_concern:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      You are on a phone call with someone who may have a safety problem with their Toyota.
      Work out which one situation applies and record it in safety_class. The steps after
      this one do and say everything else, so the moment you record safety_class you say
      nothing more. Record a value by saving it with your session context tool, never by
      saying it to the caller.
      {{#if caller_words}}What the caller said just before reaching you: "{{caller_words}}"{{/if}}
      {{#if safety_note}}Reported earlier in this call, so do not ask for it again: {{safety_note}}{{/if}}

      Go through these in order and stop at the first that fits.
      First, record injury_lockin when someone is hurt, or a child or a pet is locked in the
      car. Do it at once and ask nothing.
      Second, record roadside when the caller says the word roadside, or right now has broken
      down, has had an accident, has a car that stopped or will not start, has a flat tyre,
      is stuck on the road, or wants recovery or a tow truck. Do it at once and ask nothing.
      Third, when the caller asks for a person, ask nothing more. Record emergency if what
      they have told you already makes it one, otherwise record wants_person.
      Fourth, for a warning light or dashboard message, a leak, smoke, a smell, a noise, a
      brake or steering problem, or fear of driving, understand it first. Ask only what you
      do not know yet, one short question per turn and never more than two questions in this
      step. What matters is what they see, hear or smell, whether the car is moving or
      stopped and they are somewhere safe, and whether they feel the car is safe to drive.
      Then record emergency when the caller says the car is not safe to drive, is not sure,
      or is afraid to drive it, or when there is smoke, fire, a burning smell, fluid pouring
      out, an overheating engine, or brakes or steering that do not work properly. Record
      service_due when it is only a routine reminder that a service is due, such as a
      maintenance required or service due message, and the caller reports nothing else
      wrong. Record safe_to_drive when the caller says the car drives normally and is safe
      to drive, and simply wants it looked at.
      Fifth, record not_safety when the caller has no safety matter after all.

      Keep to these rules.
      If the caller names a light or a message and you cannot tell whether it is a routine
      service reminder, look it up once in the approved content. If that does not settle it,
      go by what the caller tells you about the car, and when the caller is not sure it is
      emergency.
      Only the caller can say the car is safe to drive. Never say so yourself, never diagnose
      the fault and never give repair or driving advice.
      If you did not understand an answer, ask again in simpler words, within the two
      questions. Never guess. If you still cannot tell after two questions, do not ask a
      third: record unclear, and a person takes the call.
      A request that has nothing to do with safety, such as a booking, a price or opening
      hours, is not yours. Do not answer it and do not decline it. Hand the caller's message
      back with the __return_to_parent__ tool and say in it that there is no safety matter.
      If you do not have that tool, or the same message reaches you again after you handed
      it back, record not_safety. When the caller has a safety matter and another request,
      deal with the safety matter only.
      Record safety_note before safety_class or together with it. It is one or two plain
      English sentences with what the caller reported, close to their own words, and whether
      the car is moving or stopped. If the caller has said where the car is, record that
      place in caller_location as an area, road or landmark in English letters. If they have
      not said it, leave caller_location empty and do not ask for it here. Record
      safety_class last, because recording it ends this step.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [search_toyota_knowledge]
    EXIT_WHEN: safety_class != "pending"
    MAX_TURNS: 5
    MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3
    ON_EXHAUSTED: triage_not_finished
    VOICE:
      END_OF_SPEECH_TURN_TYPE: complex_explanation
    THEN: drop_unused_markers

  # A marker that arrived while one of the two reasoning steps held the call (a kept thread,
  # see understand_concern) was not needed: the reasoning step has sorted the call. It is put
  # back here so that no later entry finds it. The fixed routing below then runs on the
  # recorded value.
  drop_unused_markers:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_injury = false
      entry_roadside = false
    THEN: route_not_safety

  # Fixed routing on the recorded value: one value, one path.
  # Q02: no safety matter after all. This is decided before the note is filled in, and
  # close_no_action puts the note back as it came in, so that an unrelated request is never
  # returned to the supervisor as a safety note.
  route_not_safety:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "not_safety"
    ON_FAIL: keep_safety_note
    THEN: close_no_action

  # Q02: the note for the centre, the roadside team and the supervisor is never empty. When
  # the reasoning step left it empty, the caller's last words are kept as they were said.
  keep_safety_note:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      safety_note = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(safety_note, recent_input, "The caller reported a possible safety problem. Their own words were not captured.")
    THEN: route_roadside

  # E01: roadside goes straight to the transfer; no question and no tool call stand in between.
  route_roadside:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "roadside"
    ON_FAIL: route_injury
    THEN: demo_gate

  # N22: someone hurt, or a child or a pet locked in the car.
  route_injury:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "injury_lockin"
    ON_FAIL: route_emergency
    THEN: injury_script_gate

  # Q02: emergency.
  route_emergency:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "emergency"
    ON_FAIL: route_service_due
    THEN: emergency_contact

  # Q02: service-due alert.
  route_service_due:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "service_due"
    ON_FAIL: route_safe_to_drive
    THEN: close_book_service

  # Q02: a concern the caller says is safe to drive.
  route_safe_to_drive:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "safe_to_drive"
    ON_FAIL: route_wants_person
    THEN: close_note_concern

  # The caller asks for a person while reporting a concern: a person takes the call.
  route_wants_person:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "wants_person"
    ON_FAIL: route_unclear
    THEN: person_asked_demo_gate

  # Journey 09 (E122): in the demonstration a caller who asks for a person hears the close
  # line. It is said here, by this agent's own close step, and not after a hand-over: the
  # hand-over to a person is one way, so an end_call set by the handover agent would never
  # reach the supervisor, the line would be said and the session would stay open. Said here,
  # end_call goes back to the supervisor whenever the supervisor routed the caller to this
  # agent. Any value but the string true takes the road to a person.
  person_asked_demo_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: ("{{env.TOYOTA_DEMO_MODE}}" == "true")
    ON_FAIL: raise_person_asked
    THEN: demo_close

  # Q02: still not understood after two questions. A value outside the known list ends the
  # same way: it is never read as "no action", a person takes the call.
  route_unclear:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "unclear"
    ON_FAIL: agent_failed
    THEN: raise_person_triage

  # OPEN N22 (contact centre): How often does the contact centre get this call?
  # Interim behaviour as the document states it: emergency services first, then roadside.
  # The line is said unless the flag holds the string false, so a flag that is missing or
  # mistyped keeps the line. With the flag off the caller goes straight to roadside, as in E01.
  injury_script_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: ("{{env.TOYOTA_SAFETY_INJURY_LOCKIN_SCRIPT}}" != "false")
    ON_FAIL: demo_gate
    THEN: emergency_services_first

  # N22: fixed wording. It is the one line that differs from the voice profile (barge-in is
  # allowed everywhere else): it is played in full before the roadside line, because a caller
  # who talks over it would miss the instruction that matters most.
  emergency_services_first:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "If you have not called the emergency services yet, please call them first, straight away."
    MESSAGE_KEY: emergency_services_first
    VOICE:
      BARGE_IN: disallow
    THEN: demo_gate

  # Q02: the emergency path. The two requests (walk-in to the centre, recovery details to the
  # roadside team) need a number the caller can be reached on: the contact number confirmed or
  # given on this call, otherwise the number they are calling from. The caller's own name goes
  # with the requests when they gave one.
  emergency_contact:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      walkin_mobile = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(contact_mobile, caller_phone, "")
      walkin_contact_name = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(caller_name, "")
      recovery_details_due = true
    THEN: emergency_mobile_gate

  # Q02: without a number both requests are skipped and the caller goes straight to roadside;
  # no number is asked for in an emergency.
  emergency_mobile_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: walkin_mobile IS SET AND walkin_mobile != ""
    ON_FAIL: skip_walkin_no_mobile
    THEN: emergency_name_gate

  # Q02: the name on the profile comes from the silent lookup of the calling number and is not
  # confirmed until the caller has been identified on this call. It goes to the teams only when
  # the caller is the profile holder and has been identified (matched or confirmed), and the
  # caller's own name always comes first. A caller who rings for the owner is never given the
  # owner's name. Nobody is asked for a name here.
  emergency_name_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: identity_status == "matched" OR identity_status == "confirmed"
    ON_FAIL: emergency_location_gate
    THEN: emergency_name_on_file

  emergency_name_on_file:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      walkin_contact_name = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(caller_name, customer_name, "")
    THEN: emergency_location_gate

  # Q02: the nearest centre needs a place. It is asked only when the caller has not said it.
  emergency_location_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: caller_location IS SET AND caller_location != ""
    ON_FAIL: ask_location
    THEN: find_nearest_centre

  # Q02: one question for the place. MAX_ATTEMPTS 2 = the turn that asks plus one answer; a
  # missing place never holds up recovery (a caller who cannot say where the car is goes
  # to roadside at once). A caller who asks for a person here has already been sorted as an
  # emergency: the people they reach are the roadside team, at once and at any hour, not the
  # contact centre queue. The caller can also change the picture here; the fixed routing
  # then runs again on the new value. The tool list keeps the transfer and the requests to
  # the teams out of the model's reach; no tool is needed in this step.
  ask_location:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      The caller's car may not be safe to drive and help is being arranged. One detail is
      missing, which is where the car is right now.
      Reported so far: {{safety_note}}
      Ask one short question, where is the car right now, which area, road or nearby
      landmark. When the caller names a place, record it in caller_location as an area, road
      or landmark in English letters, for example Al Quoz or near Mall of the Emirates, and
      say nothing more, because the next step speaks. Record the place even when the caller
      also asks for a tow truck.
      Ask for nothing else. Do not explain what happens next, do not give repair or driving
      advice, and do not deal with or hand back any other request here. No tool is needed in
      this step. Record a value by saving it with your session context tool, never by saying
      it to the caller.
      If the caller cannot or will not say where the car is, or asks for a person instead of
      answering, do not ask again. Record roadside in safety_class, so that the roadside
      team takes over at once.
      If the caller now tells you the situation is different, record the new value in
      safety_class instead and say nothing more. Use injury_lockin when someone is hurt or a
      child or a pet is locked in the car, service_due when it was only a routine service
      reminder, safe_to_drive when they say the car is safe to drive after all, and
      not_safety when there is no safety matter.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [search_toyota_knowledge]
    EXIT_WHEN: (caller_location IS SET AND caller_location != "") OR safety_class != "emergency"
    MAX_TURNS: 3
    MAX_ATTEMPTS: 2
    ON_EXHAUSTED: skip_walkin_no_location
    VOICE:
      END_OF_SPEECH_TURN_TYPE: open_ended_question
    THEN: drop_unused_markers

  # Q02: the nearest centre that is open at this moment and takes an unsafe car without a
  # booking (capability emergency_walkin). The model of the car is passed when known. No hold
  # line is spoken here: the runtime plays the filler while the systems answer. Whatever goes
  # wrong in this step or the next, the caller still goes to roadside (skip_walkin_failed).
  # A place that the centre finder cannot pin to one emirate (emirate_needed) counts as no
  # centre found: a centre that may be the wrong one is never alerted and never named to the
  # caller, and the caller is not asked a second question about the place.
  find_nearest_centre:
    REASONING: false
    CALL: find_service_centres
      WITH:
        area_or_landmark: caller_location
        capability: "emergency_walkin"
        open_now: true
        vehicle_model: COALESCE(vehicle_model, "")
      AS: centre_search
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: centre_search.total > 0 AND centre_search.emirate_needed == false
        THEN: read_nearest_centre
      - ELSE:
        THEN: skip_walkin_no_centre
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: skip_walkin_failed
    ON_ERROR:
      - TYPE: timeout_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE
      - TYPE: unknown_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE

  # The centre finder names the nearest centre in two flat fields.
  read_nearest_centre:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      walkin_centre_id = centre_search.nearest_centre_id
      walkin_centre_name = centre_search.nearest_centre_name
    THEN: check_centre_found

  check_centre_found:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: walkin_centre_id IS SET AND walkin_centre_id != ""
    ON_FAIL: skip_walkin_no_centre
    THEN: send_walkin_request

  # Q02: the emergency walk-in request. The gates above set every required input. The centre
  # is also told where the car is.
  send_walkin_request:
    REASONING: false
    CALL: send_emergency_walkin_request
      WITH:
        centre_id: walkin_centre_id
        issue_summary: safety_note
        customer_mobile: walkin_mobile
        plate_number: COALESCE(plate_number, "")
        customer_name: COALESCE(walkin_contact_name, "")
        location: caller_location
      AS: walkin_request
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: walkin_request.sent == true
        THEN: confirm_walkin_sent
      - ELSE:
        THEN: skip_walkin_failed
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: skip_walkin_failed
    ON_ERROR:
      - TYPE: timeout_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE
      - TYPE: unknown_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE

  confirm_walkin_sent:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      walkin_status = "sent"
    RESPOND: "I've told our {{walkin_centre_name}} service centre that your car is coming in."
    MESSAGE_KEY: walkin_request_sent
    THEN: demo_gate

  # Q02: when the walk-in request cannot be sent, recovery still goes to the roadside team.
  # With no number to give, the recovery details cannot be sent either.
  skip_walkin_no_mobile:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      walkin_status = "not_sent_no_mobile"
      recovery_details_due = false
    THEN: demo_gate

  skip_walkin_no_location:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      walkin_status = "not_sent_no_location"
    THEN: demo_gate

  skip_walkin_no_centre:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      walkin_status = "not_sent_no_centre"
    THEN: demo_gate

  # A system has just failed. No second system is waited for before the transfer, so the
  # recovery details are not sent by message either.
  skip_walkin_failed:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      walkin_status = "not_sent_system_failed"
      recovery_details_due = false
    THEN: demo_gate

  # Journey 09 (E122): no live transfer at the AI Summit, and no recovery request to the
  # roadside team. Any value but the string true transfers.
  demo_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: ("{{env.TOYOTA_DEMO_MODE}}" == "true")
    ON_FAIL: roadside_request_gate
    THEN: demo_close

  # Q02 "passes recovery to the roadside team": for a concern sorted as an emergency the
  # details (what the caller reported, where the car is, the centre that was alerted, the
  # number to call) go to the roadside team by message just before the live transfer, so that
  # the roadside team does not have to ask for them again. A caller who says roadside or
  # reports an injury (E01, N22) has given no such details and is transferred at once.
  roadside_request_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: recovery_details_due == true
    ON_FAIL: start_transfer
    THEN: prepare_roadside_request

  # The request is tried once only: the flag is put back before the call, so no recovery road
  # can come round to it again.
  prepare_roadside_request:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      recovery_details_due = false
      recovery_summary = "The caller reported a safety problem that may make their Toyota unsafe to drive and is being transferred to the roadside team for recovery. Emergency walk-in request to a service centre: " + walkin_status + ". Service centre: " + FIRST_NON_EMPTY(walkin_centre_name, "none") + ". Reported by the caller: " + FIRST_NON_EMPTY(safety_note, "not captured")
    THEN: send_roadside_request

  # Q02: the recovery request. Whatever comes back, the next step is the transfer: a request
  # that fails or is refused never blocks or delays it, and nothing is said about it. No
  # callback is asked for: the caller is on the line and is transferred live.
  send_roadside_request:
    REASONING: false
    CALL: send_team_request
      WITH:
        team: "roadside"
        request_type: "roadside_recovery"
        summary: recovery_summary
        customer_mobile: walkin_mobile
        customer_name: COALESCE(walkin_contact_name, "")
        plate_number: COALESCE(plate_number, "")
        callback_requested: false
        location: caller_location
      AS: roadside_request
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: roadside_request.sent == true
        THEN: note_roadside_request_sent
      - ELSE:
        THEN: start_transfer
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: start_transfer
    ON_ERROR:
      - TYPE: timeout_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE
      - TYPE: unknown_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE

  note_roadside_request_sent:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      roadside_request_status = "sent"
    THEN: start_transfer

  # Every road to the live transfer passes here. The transfer is started once per visit: if
  # anything fails after this point a person takes over (recovery_after_transfer).
  start_transfer:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      transfer_tried = true
    THEN: transfer_roadside

  # E01, N22, Q02: live transfer to the roadside team. No hours check: it runs at any hour.
  # The destination is deployment configuration; the caller hears the shared roadside line.
  # The platform does not run a call whose spoken line has no text for the caller's language,
  # so that one case is caught first and the transfer is made without the localised line.
  # Only a result that says the transfer succeeded counts as connected. Every other result,
  # and every way the call can fail, ends in transfer_failed and from there with a person: a
  # caller is never left waiting on a transfer that did not happen.
  transfer_roadside:
    REASONING: false
    CALL: call_transfer
      WITH:
        callTransferType: "sip"
        message: "{{locale.connecting_to_roadside}}"
      AS: roadside_transfer
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: roadside_transfer.error.code == "LOCALE_KEY_MISSING"
        THEN: transfer_roadside_plain
      - IF: roadside_transfer.success == true
        THEN: roadside_connected
      - ELSE:
        THEN: transfer_failed
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: transfer_failed
    ON_ERROR:
      - TYPE: routing_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE
      - TYPE: timeout_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE
      - TYPE: unknown_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE

  # E01: the roadside transfer never waits for wording. The line is said from its default text
  # and the call is transferred with no spoken line of its own.
  transfer_roadside_plain:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I'm connecting you to our roadside team now. Please stay on the line."
    MESSAGE_KEY: connecting_to_roadside
    CALL: call_transfer
      WITH:
        callTransferType: "sip"
      AS: roadside_transfer_plain
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: roadside_transfer_plain.success == true
        THEN: roadside_connected
      - ELSE:
        THEN: transfer_failed
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: transfer_failed
    ON_ERROR:
      - TYPE: routing_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE
      - TYPE: timeout_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE
      - TYPE: unknown_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE

  roadside_connected:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      safety_outcome = "emergency_handled"
    THEN: COMPLETE

  # E01, N22, Q02: the roadside transfer did not go through. The caller hears that once, is
  # given the roadside team's own number when it is on file, and a person then takes over
  # with the full picture (raise_person_transfer).
  transfer_failed:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry, I couldn't reach our roadside team just now."
    MESSAGE_KEY: roadside_transfer_failed
    THEN: find_roadside_number

  # The roadside number is data: it is looked up, never written in this file. When the lookup
  # finds nothing or fails, no number is said and the person takes over all the same.
  find_roadside_number:
    REASONING: false
    CALL: get_contact_number
      WITH:
        contact_key: "roadside"
      AS: roadside_contact
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: roadside_contact.found == true AND roadside_contact.phone_number != ""
        THEN: keep_roadside_number
      - ELSE:
        THEN: raise_person_transfer
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: raise_person_transfer
    ON_ERROR:
      - TYPE: timeout_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE
      - TYPE: unknown_error
        RETRY: 0
        THEN: CONTINUE

  # A space after every digit, so that the number is read out digit by digit in both languages.
  keep_roadside_number:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      roadside_number_spoken = TRIM(REGEX_REPLACE(roadside_contact.phone_number, "([0-9])", "$1 "))
    THEN: say_roadside_number

  say_roadside_number:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "You can reach our roadside team directly on {{roadside_number_spoken}}."
    MESSAGE_KEY: roadside_number
    VOICE:
      INSTRUCTIONS: "Calm and clear. Read the phone number slowly, one digit at a time."
    THEN: raise_person_transfer

  # Journey 09 (E122): the demo close line instead of the live transfer, and for a caller who
  # asked for a person in the demonstration. end_call goes back to the supervisor, which ends
  # the call; the outcome that goes with it is not read after that.
  demo_close:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      safety_outcome = "emergency_handled"
      end_call = true
    RESPOND: "That's the end of this demonstration, and thank you for trying the Toyota voice assistant. For anything further, please speak to the team at the Toyota stand."
    MESSAGE_KEY: demo_close
    THEN: COMPLETE

  # Q02: a service-due alert goes back so that a normal service can be booked. The line
  # offers the booking and leaves the next request to the supervisor.
  close_book_service:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      safety_outcome = "book_service"
    RESPOND: "That sounds like a routine reminder that a service is due. We can book that service for you now, if you'd like."
    MESSAGE_KEY: service_reminder_close
    THEN: COMPLETE

  # Q02: a concern the caller says is safe to drive goes back as a note for the centre.
  close_note_concern:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      safety_outcome = "note_concern"
    RESPOND: "Thanks, I've noted that. We can book a visit now so the service centre can look at it, if you'd like."
    MESSAGE_KEY: concern_noted_close
    THEN: COMPLETE

  # No safety matter: the note goes back exactly as it came in (empty unless a real concern
  # was reported earlier on this call), whatever was written about the unrelated request. It
  # is always written, as an empty text when there was none, so that the supervisor's copy is
  # overwritten. The supervisor adds nothing after the return, so the turn is closed here
  # with the shared question.
  close_no_action:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      safety_note = COALESCE(note_at_entry, "")
      safety_outcome = "no_action"
    RESPOND: "Is there anything else I can help you with?"
    MESSAGE_KEY: anything_else
    THEN: COMPLETE

  # Last resort: a recovery road was needed a second time in the same visit, or the hand-over
  # to a person could not be reached. The caller hears that once and the call goes back to the
  # supervisor. No tool, no model call and no hand-over happen here, so this step cannot fail
  # again, and the flag is put back so that no hand-over is tried once more behind it. The
  # caller is not left in silence: the shared question follows, and a caller who asks for
  # roadside again is routed here afresh.
  close_unrecovered:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      needs_person = false
      safety_outcome = "no_action"
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry, I couldn't connect you just now."
    MESSAGE_KEY: could_not_connect
    THEN: ask_anything_else

  ask_anything_else:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "Is there anything else I can help you with?"
    MESSAGE_KEY: anything_else
    THEN: COMPLETE

  # Recovery road 1. The reasoning step could not finish: the question limit was reached, the
  # model call failed or a step timed out. What is already known decides, with no further
  # question and no model call. Both recovery roads count their visits in recovery_count: a
  # second visit means the recovery itself failed, and the flow stops instead of going round.
  # The recovery details are not sent by message on this road: the transfer comes first.
  triage_not_finished:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      recovery_count = ADD(COALESCE(recovery_count, 0), 1)
      recovery_details_due = false
    CHECK: recovery_count < 2
    ON_FAIL: close_unrecovered
    THEN: recovery_after_transfer

  # E01, N22, Q02: the live transfer was already started in this visit and something failed
  # after it. It is not started a second time: a person takes over.
  recovery_after_transfer:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: transfer_tried == true
    ON_FAIL: triage_known_injury
    THEN: raise_person_transfer

  # N22: a caller already sorted as injury or lock-in still hears the emergency services line.
  triage_known_injury:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "injury_lockin"
    ON_FAIL: triage_known_class
    THEN: injury_script_gate

  # E01, Q02: a caller already sorted for roadside or as an emergency still gets roadside;
  # everyone else gets a person.
  triage_known_class:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "roadside" OR safety_class == "emergency"
    ON_FAIL: raise_person_triage
    THEN: demo_gate

  # Recovery road 2. An unexpected failure, or a recorded value outside the known list: the
  # caller hears the shared apology, then what is already known decides, as on road 1.
  agent_failed:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      recovery_count = ADD(COALESCE(recovery_count, 0), 1)
      recovery_details_due = false
    CHECK: recovery_count < 2
    ON_FAIL: close_unrecovered
    THEN: say_system_trouble

  # The shared apology promises nothing: the handover agent says the connecting line.
  say_system_trouble:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry, I'm having trouble with that just now."
    MESSAGE_KEY: system_trouble
    THEN: error_after_transfer

  # E01, N22, Q02: when the failure came after the live transfer was started, the person is
  # told that the caller still needs roadside (the urgent reason), not only that something failed.
  error_after_transfer:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: transfer_tried == true
    ON_FAIL: error_known_injury
    THEN: raise_person_transfer

  # N22, E01, Q02: a caller already sorted as injury or lock-in, for roadside or as an
  # emergency still gets roadside after an unexpected failure; everyone else gets a person.
  error_known_injury:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "injury_lockin"
    ON_FAIL: error_known_class
    THEN: injury_script_gate

  error_known_class:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: safety_class == "roadside" OR safety_class == "emergency"
    ON_FAIL: raise_person_error
    THEN: demo_gate

  # The four roads to a person. Each records why a person is needed and what that person has
  # to know; the summary ends with the caller's own report so that nothing is asked again.
  # The shared step hand_to_person then sets the flag and hands the call over.
  # E01, N22, Q02: the roadside transfer failed. The handover agent treats this reason as
  # urgent (the roadside queue, no callback offer).
  raise_person_transfer:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      handover_reason = "roadside_transfer_failed"
      handover_summary = "The caller needs the Toyota roadside team and the live transfer to roadside failed. Emergency walk-in request to a service centre: " + walkin_status + ". Nearest centre found: " + FIRST_NON_EMPTY(walkin_centre_name, "none") + ". Recovery details sent to the roadside team by message: " + roadside_request_status + ". Where the car is: " + FIRST_NON_EMPTY(caller_location, "not given") + ". Please connect the caller to roadside help or arrange recovery now. Reported by the caller: " + FIRST_NON_EMPTY(safety_note, recent_input, "not captured")
    THEN: hand_to_person

  # Q02: the concern was still unclear after two questions, or the model call failed.
  raise_person_triage:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      handover_reason = "safety_concern_unclear"
      handover_summary = "The caller reported a possible safety problem with their Toyota and the assistant could not work out how serious it is. Please find out whether the car is safe to drive and arrange roadside help if it is not. Reported by the caller: " + FIRST_NON_EMPTY(safety_note, recent_input, "not captured")
    THEN: hand_to_person

  # The caller asked for a person.
  raise_person_asked:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      handover_reason = "caller_asked"
      handover_summary = "The caller asked for a person while reporting a possible safety problem with their Toyota. Please check whether the car is safe to drive and whether roadside help is needed. Reported by the caller: " + FIRST_NON_EMPTY(safety_note, recent_input, "not captured")
    THEN: hand_to_person

  # The assistant failed before the concern was handled.
  raise_person_error:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      handover_reason = "safety_agent_error"
      handover_summary = "The caller reported a possible safety problem with their Toyota or asked for roadside help and the assistant failed before it was handled. Please find out what they need and arrange roadside help if the car is not safe to drive. Reported by the caller: " + FIRST_NON_EMPTY(safety_note, recent_input, "not captured")
    THEN: hand_to_person

  # The escape itself. The reason and the summary are already set by the step before, so the
  # hand-over carries them whatever order the two lines below run in. The flag is set and the
  # hand-off is made in this one step; the flow never completes with the flag raised.
  hand_to_person:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      needs_person = true
    DO:
      - HANDOFF: Toyota_Human_Handover_Agent

# The escape to a person. The whole conversation goes with it. This agent holds no booking
# reference and sets no queue: the handover agent takes the roadside queue itself when the
# reason is roadside_transfer_failed, and the service queue otherwise.
HANDOFF:
  - TO: Toyota_Human_Handover_Agent
    WHEN: needs_person == true
    CONTEXT:
      pass: [caller_phone, contact_mobile, caller_name, crm_customer_id, customer_name, identity_status, plate_number, vehicle_model, handover_reason, handover_summary]
      summary: "{{handover_summary}}"
      history: full
    EXPECT_RETURN: false

# Errors. The tool steps of the emergency path carry handlers of their own (a list of TYPE
# entries, the form the compiler reads on a step). They treat every kind of error in the step
# as a failed call, so the step's own ON_FAILURE decides: after the centre search, the walk-in
# request or the recovery request the caller goes on to the transfer; after the transfer the
# caller hears the apology and the roadside number and a person takes over; after the number
# lookup the person takes over. The handlers below cover every other step.
ON_ERROR:
  # Tool failures are handled by the ON_FAILURE branch of the step that made the call. The
  # tool library already retries once, so there is no second retry here. A tool argument that
  # fails validation is treated the same way.
  tool_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: CONTINUE

  validation_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: CONTINUE

  # A failed model call: one retry, then what is already known decides (roadside or a person).
  # A step that timed out is handled the same way, without a retry.
  llm_error:
    RETRY: 1
    THEN: BACKTRACK
    BACKTRACK_TO: triage_not_finished

  timeout_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: BACKTRACK
    BACKTRACK_TO: triage_not_finished

  # Anything unexpected: the apology, then roadside for a caller already sorted for it, and a
  # person for everyone else.
  unknown_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: BACKTRACK
    BACKTRACK_TO: agent_failed

  # The hand-over to a person could not be reached: stop cleanly, back to the supervisor.
  routing_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: BACKTRACK
    BACKTRACK_TO: close_unrecovered
